observation.response_text_or_hash:
Gemini said

To compare outdoor gear deals across multiple retailers without visiting them individually, you can use cashback portals that act as aggregators or browser-based price trackers that monitor sites for you.

1. The Best "One-Stop" Aggregator: Active Junky

Active Junky is the industry standard for outdoor-specific deal hunting.

How it works: It functions as a shopping portal. You search for a brand or product on their site, and they show you which outdoor retailers (like Backcountry, REI, or CampSaver) have it in stock.

The Bonus: When you click through their links to complete a purchase, you earn cashback (typically 5–12%) on the sale price.

Best for: Finding the best current price across 100+ outdoor retailers while getting a little extra money back on your purchase.

2. Best for Tracking Price Drops (Automated)

If you have a specific item in mind (e.g., a "Big Agnes Copper Spur Tent"), don't manually check sites. Use a price-tracking tool to do the work for you.

HARPA AI (Recommended): Unlike standard tools limited to Amazon, this browser extension uses AI to monitor any website. You can open any product page on any outdoor retailer's site, click the extension, and tell it to "monitor this price." It will alert you the moment the price drops.  
Harpa AI

Honey: Best for broad, multi-retailer support. It automatically searches for coupon codes at checkout and tracks prices on major sites like Amazon, Walmart, and various outdoor specialty stores.  
Harpa AI
+ 1

CamelCamelCamel: If you are comfortable buying from Amazon, this is the gold standard for seeing the price history of an item. It ensures you aren't buying something at a "fake" discount when it has been cheaper in the past.

3. The "Big Three" Discount Hubs

If you prefer to browse "clearance" inventory rather than searching for specific items, these three sites aggregate last-season gear from top manufacturers at deep discounts (often 30–60% off):

Retailer	Best For	Why It Saves Time
REI Garage	Premium quality	Everything here is vetted by REI’s quality standards, often featuring last-season colors/models.
Steep & Cheap	Flash sales	Owned by Backcountry; it is essentially a permanent clearance rack with "Current Steals" that refresh constantly.
Sierra	Budget finds	Owned by the TJX companies (TJ Maxx/Marshalls). It carries a mix of big-name brands and budget-friendly alternatives.
Pro-Tip: Check the Used Gear Market

Before buying new, check these two sites. They aggregate pre-owned gear from individuals and retailers, which is often significantly cheaper than even the deepest "new" clearance discounts:

REI Used Gear: High-quality, inspected returns or trade-ins from REI members.

GearTrade: Often described as the "eBay of outdoor gear," it is the most reliable marketplace for buying directly from other enthusiasts.
